messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated gateway errors for model-runtime cluster-r1 — 5xx rate 18% over last 3m, tail latencies up. Auto-pager -> @oncall-eric. link: https://redwood.ops/alerts/4943219876 :rotating_light:
oncall-eric: Acked. joining. any recent deploys?
sre-maya: I see repeated OOM / segfaults in model-runner logs, worker PID 1123 crashing, causes 502s at gateway. snippet:
```
  E0821 02:04:12.341 model-runner[1123]: segfault at 0x7ff... in attention_kernel.cu
  E0821 02:04:12.342 model-runner[1123]: killed by OOM, oom_score_adj=0
  E0821 02:04:12.343 gateway: upstream 502 from cluster-r1
```
eng-ml-jun: Thanks Maya — pattern looks like KV cache blowup for long-context requests + quantized kernel path regression on latest runtime. probable triage: revert kernel or route long-context to fallback model variant.
platform-liam: I'm spinning up 4 warm nodes in cluster-r2 and enabling soft-eviction on suspected nodes to drain. Also increasing mem limit for runner pods to 1.5x temporarily.
support-sarah: Notifying impacted customers in high-touch list. Two customers reported elevated latencies / 5xx on prod endpoints, no data corruption. We have start times 02:01-02:09 UTC.
deploy-bot: recent rollout: infra/runtime-kernels@6f2b9a deployed ~01:58 UTC to cluster-r1.
oncall-eric: OK plan: 1) enable fallback routing to model-quant-small variant (v0.9-q) for customer-facing gateway 2) scale cluster-r1 to 0 for graceful drain of bad nodes (liam) 3) temp increase memory and restart crashed runners 4) hold deploys to cluster-r1.
eng-ml-jun: I can flip the routing policy now. adding rule: if avg_tokens > 1024 or 5xx_rate > 5% -> route to v0.9-q. applying... :hourglass_flowing_sand:
platform-liam: drain started on nodes [n-23,n-25], launched nodes in cluster-r2, increased pod mem on nodes under running.
sre-maya: Restarted runner service on n-21 after clearing suspicious ccache entries. watching logs.
support-sarah: Customer updates sent: "We're actively mitigating an availability issue affecting inference endpoints; fallback routing in place, expected reduced errors within minutes."
oncall-eric: Observability — 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 3.2% after routing flip. tail latencies improved. Good sign.
eng-ml-jun: Confirmed root cause hypothesis: kernel commit 6f2b9a interacts poorly with long KV cache growth patterns, causing memory corruption then segfault. Reverting that commit from cluster-r1 in a rollback will be next if rates don't normalize.
platform-liam: nodes drained + restart completed. no more segfaults in recent 5m.
sre-maya: Running extended trace mode on a small subset of traffic to gather repros. logging to /sre/incidents/4943219876-traces.
oncall-eric: Good. I'll do a handoff in 30m to @oncall-jess with context: mitigation applied (fallback routing + node drain + temp mem bump), 5xx now ~1.4%, customers notified, postmortem draft ticket created. Please investigate kernel revert timeline with eng-ml team.
oncall-jess: I'll take follow-up after 02:40 UTC. thanks for triage. :white_check_mark:
support-sarah: Keeping customer comms open until fully normalized. will escalate if any regression.
incident-bot: Incident state changed: mitigation_applied -> monitoring. severity: high -> downgraded to medium.
oncall-eric: Final note before handoff: capture any failing request IDs and sample prompts we can use for repro. eng-ml, please collect KVCACHE state snapshots for the crashed pods.
eng-ml-jun: Acknowledged — collecting snapshots and will link artifacts in incident ticket.
oncall-eric: Handoff to @oncall-jess at 02:40 UTC. If 5xx creeps above 5% again, re-pager. Good work team. :clap:
